subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to diagnostics for dropped Telegram `MEDIA:` directives while root expansion stays with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002, or should this issue also change the host-local media root policy?
rationale: Changing which absolute host paths can be read and uploaded is a security boundary decision, while warning/log behavior can likely be fixed independently once maintainers choose what path details may be exposed.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
options.body: Fix warning/log behavior in this issue and keep configurable host-root policy in the canonical root-policy thread.

options.title: Own root policy here
options.body: Use this issue to define a broader Telegram local-media root contract, accepting the security-review and migration burden here.

options.title: Close as policy-only
options.body: Close this issue as covered by the existing trust-model docs and keep only the canonical root-policy issue open, leaving the diagnostics request untracked.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
recommendation.body: Fix warning/log behavior in this issue and keep configurable host-root policy in the canonical root-policy thread.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest history on the outbound media access policy and central plumbing that this decision would affect.
